Office of the Senate Sergeant-at-Arms (OSAA) acting chief Mao Aplasca on Friday explained his move to fire a warning shot during the May 13 gunfire incident inside the building in Pasay City. Aplasca said OSAA personnel first challenged the armed individuals, asked them to identify themselves and ordered them to lower their firearms, but they did not do so.

data.text:
A Reddit post criticizing Meralco’s push for tighter regulation on “guerilla” solar setups is gaining traction after a user described how residents in their area allegedly had to repair burned electrical wires themselves following a fire linked to overloaded “spaghetti wires.” The post, shared in the subreddit r/Philippines, argued that stricter solar requirements could make installations even more expensive and inaccessible while long-standing electrical hazards in some communities remain unresolved.

The viral discussion has centered on why solar users are facing tighter scrutiny while dangerous wiring conditions remain visible in many neighborhoods. The user pointed out that solar panel installations in the Philippines already undergo permits, inspections, and net metering approvals before they can legally connect to the grid.

Meralco, however, said its call for standardized solar regulations is focused on safety rather than control or opposition to renewable energy adoption. The utility warned that uncoordinated solar installations can cause backfeeding, voltage fluctuations, equipment damage, and risks to line crews working on supposedly de-energized power lines.

The post nevertheless reflects broader frustrations over electricity costs, aging infrastructure, and consumer access to alternative energy sources, with some users questioning why visible grid hazards continue to persist while additional safeguards are being pushed more aggressively on solar adopters.
